diet.text: Small reptiles, frogs, birds and mammals

overview.text: The Oriental (or Indian) Rat Snake is a large, fast, non-venomous snake of South and South-east Asia. It is one of the longest colubrid snakes in the world.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually about 1.5 to 1.95 m and fairly slender; some are over 2 m, and the record is 3.7 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: From Iran, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan through Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh to southern China, Taiwan and South-east Asia as far as Java and Bali.

habitat.text: Forest floors, wetlands, rice paddies, farmland and suburbs.

behaviour.text: Active by day and partly a climber. It is fast and excitable but harmless to people. In the breeding season males wrestle by twisting their bodies around each other in a test of strength.

diet.text: Small reptiles, amphibians, birds and mammals. Unusually, adults often pin prey down with their body weight instead of squeezing it.

reproduction.text: Mates in late spring and early summer (all year round in the tropics) and lays eggs.
